# Visual plan projections and diff-grounded recaps across war-strategy, mid-run adjudication, and war-review

## Motivation

Merged plans and mid-run adjudication surfaces are dense Markdown. Operator readability suffers exactly where it matters most: reviewing a plan before ratifying it, adjudicating an escalation mid-run, and understanding what a run actually built.

[BuilderIO/skills](https://github.com/BuilderIO/skills) ships two skills worth borrowing from:

- **`/visual-plan`** — renders a forward plan as an interactive document of typed blocks (`diagram`, `data-model`, `api-endpoint`, `file-tree`, split `diff`, `annotated-code`, wireframe canvases, a bottom `question-form`), with a comment→patch→resolve review loop.
- **`/visual-recap`** — the same block model built *from* a diff: UI headline → short outcome narrative → contract deltas → `file-tree` with per-file change flags → a "Key changes" tab strip of 3–8 annotated split diffs. Its **grounding rule**: structured blocks are derived mechanically from the actual diff (real paths, real fields, real before/after text); the model writes only the prose.

## Why not adopt the skills as a hard dependency

- Both hard-depend on the Agent-Native Plans stack. Hosted default writes plan/diff content to `plan.agent-native.com`'s database — unreleased private-repo content leaving the machine, colliding with this repo's redaction posture. Local-files mode still needs the `npx @agent-native/core` CLI and renders through the hosted Plan UI via a localhost bridge; the comment/feedback loop (half the value) is hosted-only.
- WAR currently has zero runtime dependencies beyond Node ≥ 24; this would be its first external service coupling.
- **Doctrinal conflict**: visual-plan's discipline is "the document is the source of truth." In WAR, the merged plan (`docs/plans/*.md`) is the execution artifact — `/war` executes it, `/red-team` patches it in place, drift guards pin it. A visual surface can never be canonical here.
- Calibration: the skill's own Visual Surface Choice rule gives architecture/backend/data plans **no canvas and no wireframes** — document plus inline diagrams only. Nearly every WAR plan is that kind of plan, so the valuable subset is diagrams, file maps, and structured blocks, not the wireframe/prototype machinery.

## Proposed shape

Adopt the **pattern natively** (HTML/mermaid renders published as default-private Artifacts, whose comment threads the agent can read, patch against, and resolve — functionally the same loop, zero new dependencies), and pin one piece of doctrine:

> **Visual surfaces are generated one-way projections of the merged plan / landed diff — never canonical.** Feedback flows back into the `.md`; the projection is regenerated. (Same pattern as MEMORY.md: a render-index projection, never hand-edited.)

### 1. `/war-review` — "show me what was built" (first landing spot)

Post-run visual recap of the landed range: outcome narrative → `file-tree` with change flags → 3–8 annotated key-change diffs, plus the telemetry the skill already tallies. Non-blocking, diff already landed, run manifest already names everything the recap needs. Lowest risk; trials block shapes, budgets, and the grounding rule before they enter the hot path.

### 2. `/war-strategy` — plan projection

After the merged plan is written (and after every `/red-team` patch), render: Commander's Intent per phase at a glance, the phase → wave → task DAG with `deps` edges, per-task Files lists (file-disjointness — same-file collisions become literally visible), the assumptions ledger, and open questions. Doubles as the red-team grill surface. Merged `.md` stays gospel; projection regenerates on patch.

### 3. `/war` — mid-run adjudication recap

When a `held:escalation`, an `ask` strike-list gate, or a red-team blocker reaches the operator mid-run, generate a recap of `frozen-phase-base..integration-tip`: file-tree with change flags, tasks merged vs. blocked, the load-bearing diffs annotated, the finding anchored to the exact hunk. Constraints:

- The Workflow sandbox cannot invoke skills — this is a **Lead-side action at the escalation surface** (skill prose in `/war`), not a workflow-template.js change.
- Generated concurrently, never blocking, and **size-gated** — adopt the source skill's budgets verbatim (skip for small diffs; 3–8 tabs; ~150 lines per excerpt).

### 4. BuilderIO skills as an optional front door

Treat installed `/visual-plan` / `/visual-recap` the way doctrine treats the Grill Me family: *recommended front door, never a dependency*. If the operator has them installed and opts in, hand off in local-files mode only (`AGENT_NATIVE_PLANS_MODE=local-files`) — the hosted default publishes private repo content externally.

## Doctrine placement

- Per ADR 0042, the shared recap-authoring doctrine (skeleton, budgets, grounding rule) lives in one `references/` file with `when <trigger>, read references/<file>` pointers from the three consuming surfaces — not inlined three times.
- A new ADR pins "visual surfaces are one-way projections, never canonical."

## Sequencing

1. `/war-review` recap render (prototype against a recent run to judge output shape first).
2. `/war-strategy` plan projection + the projections ADR.
3. `/war` adjudication recap prose, size-gated.
4. Optional-front-door wiring for the BuilderIO skills, local-files-mode mandated.
